open-question.question: What notation do placeholders take (for example <milestone_id>, <project-root>), and where are they and the headless flags explained: in one legend section at the top of the page, or repeated beside each snippet that uses them?
open-question.alternative: Placeholders keep the notation the rest of the tree already uses for the same values, a lowercase name in angle brackets spelled as the skill reference spells it (<milestone_id> exactly as in its `specify-milestone-starting-state <milestone_id>` usage heading, <project-root> for the local path the draft's --add-dir carried), and one ## section between the page's intro paragraph and the first way, headed for what it holds rather than for a goal, explains everything once: that angle brackets mark the only text a reader substitutes while every other token runs as written, the two placeholders, the -p "/cairn:<skill>" line form, one sentence per headless flag with its per-host form, and the one-line host swap; each way then carries only its heading, its one or two sentences, and its fenced block. Under the sibling picks a placeholder sits on the odd line (the milestone id argument, the agy line's --add-dir path) while the four flags sit on every line, so the legend's bulk is page-wide material that belongs in one place: a change to either CLI's effort enum or model form is one edit, the per-way template stays the goal's three parts, a contributed way inherits the legend and adds at most one line to it, and the tokens match the 13 <milestone_id> occurrences across docs/workflow.md and docs/skill-reference.md so the same token means the same value across docs/. A reader who deep-links to one way (the draft is titled a lookup) meets a block whose flags are explained one scroll up, and a ## legend shares the heading level of the ways, so its heading and its position before the first way are what keep it from reading as a way, a structural element none of the three sibling docs pages has, since workflow.md explains its diagram notation in the paragraph that opens its pipeline section rather than in a section of its own.

The same angle-bracket notation, but each way's one-or-two-sentence intro (or a line under its block) resolves the placeholders and explains the flags its lines carry, with no page-level legend. Every way is self-contained: a reader who lands on one heading reads two sentences, substitutes, and runs, with nothing to scroll to. The flags are on every line of every way, so the four flag sentences with their per-host forms and the host swap repeat in every way (a change to either CLI's effort enum or model form is one edit per way, and a contributed way must re-author them, where they drift), and the goal fixes each way's one or two sentences to when to use it and what it yields, so the repeated explanation either crowds those out or grows the template a fourth part.

The legend section of Top legend section for the line form, the flags, and the host swap, plus a short clause in the intro of each way whose block carries a placeholder naming the value to substitute (the starting way for <milestone_id>, the mixed-agent review for <project-root>). The ways a deep-linking reader cannot run without a substitution say so on the spot, at the cost of one clause each, while the page-wide flag material stays single-sourced. Each placeholder's meaning then lives in two places to keep aligned, the clause spends part of a per-way sentence slot the goal reserves for when to use the way and what it yields, and it buys little: the two tokens name their own values, and the same deep-linking reader still needs the legend for the flags on every line.

Placeholders become shell variables: an assignment line at the top of each block that uses one (MILESTONE_ID=..., PROJECT_ROOT=... or PROJECT_ROOT="$PWD") and lines reading "/cairn:specify-milestone-starting-state $MILESTONE_ID" and --add-dir "$PROJECT_ROOT", with the flags explained in a top legend as in Top legend section. A block runs after the reader edits one assignment line instead of finding a token inside a command, and $PWD makes the mixed-agent review runnable as written from the project root. It breaks the notation the tree uses for the same values (<milestone_id> in the skill reference's usage headings and in workflow.md), adds shell-syntax lines that are not cairn mechanics and are wrong outside a POSIX shell, the assignment's right-hand side is a placeholder anyway (MILESTONE_ID=<milestone_id>), and --add-dir "$PWD" is not the value the draft verified.
open-question.recommendation: Under the sibling picks a placeholder sits on the odd line (the <milestone_id> argument, the agy line's --add-dir <project-root>) while the four flags sit on every line, so the explanation is page-wide material that belongs in one ## section between the intro and the first way, which a CLI change edits once and a contributed way inherits rather than re-authors; keeping the angle-bracket tokens the skill reference already uses lets that section state the one rule the page needs, that angle brackets are the only text a reader substitutes and everything else runs as written, and the near tie with per-way reminders breaks on the goal fixing each way's sentences to when to use it and what it yields, which leaves no slot for a note the token names already carry.

open-question.question: Which ways does the page ship with at promotion time? The draft holds six Claude Code snippets and one Antigravity block, none of which mixes hosts; the goal names a mixed-agent requirements review and putting more intelligence into a stuck milestone as examples, so the shipped list and the concrete chain of the mixed-host way need fixing.
open-question.alternative: Ship exactly the four ways the goal names as examples: starting a milestone (the draft's two first runs merged into one goto-next-milestone, specify-milestone-starting-state, review-milestone-requirements, recommend-all-open-questions chain), a mixed-agent requirements review, putting more intelligence into a stuck milestone (the draft's "Just put more intelligence and execute" chain), and executing tasks, with the draft's Finish snippet, Subsequent runs snippet, and Antigravity block shipping as no way of their own. The inventory is the goal's own list, so no section needs a justification the goal does not already give, and it is the smallest page that covers the goal. The goal introduces its list with "for example", so reading it as exhaustive drops the one verified line it omits, finish-current-milestone, and leaves the page ending at complete-all-tasks with no way to close a milestone, sending the reader back to the skill reference for the last step.

Promote every draft snippet as its own way, the six Claude Code snippets plus the Antigravity block under a heading invented for it, each generalized in place, and add the mixed-agent requirements review as an eighth way beside them. The closest match to milestone 26's word-for-word promotion: every chain the draft verified ships as the section it was run as, and no consolidation judgment is made at promotion time. Under the Host per line layout host, model, and effort are per-line values, so the two first runs (one chain under two value sets), the Subsequent runs snippet beside the mixed-agent review (one loop pass with and without a host swap), and the Antigravity block (the subsequent-runs and execute chains with the host swapped) are the same ways written two or three times, contradicting the goal-oriented organization, and the unheaded Antigravity block ending in an empty agy -p "" line has no goal to name.

Five ways in pipeline order, one per goal the draft chained: starting a milestone (the two first runs merged into one goto-next-milestone, specify-milestone-starting-state with its milestone id argument, review-milestone-requirements, recommend-all-open-questions chain, keeping the Fable-based run's per-line model mix because it is the one of the two that mixes models within the chain), a mixed-agent requirements review (the loop pass with its concrete chain fixed as review-milestone-requirements on agy carrying --add-dir on the project root and the permissions flag, the flags the draft's Antigravity block ran, then recommend-all-open-questions on claude at --model opus --effort max, then answer-all-open-questions-with-recommendation on claude at --model opus --effort high, repeated until review reports convergence), putting more intelligence into a stuck milestone (the draft's six-line "Just put more intelligence and execute" chain), executing tasks (the draft's Execute tasks chain), and finishing a milestone (the draft's one-line Finish snippet); the Subsequent runs snippet and the Antigravity block ship inside the mixed-agent review as its single-host reading through the legend's host swap. Every goal the draft chained ships exactly once under a heading naming it, the goal's mixed-agent review becomes the canonical loop pass, and every line of the mixed chain is copied from the snippet that verified it on that host (the Antigravity block's review line, the Claude Code chains' recommend and answer lines), so the page claims no flag or value that never ran while the chain itself rests on the commit-per-skill property the starting state records as what makes host mixing safe. Two of the five are consolidations the draft never ran as written: the merged starting way demotes the all-opus first run to a sentence, and the mixed-agent chain was verified line by line but never end to end, so its first end-to-end run is the reader's; Antigravity then appears on one shipped line, the rest of that host's verified lines living only in the legend's swap rule.

Four ways mirroring the headless-capable phases of docs/workflow.md, initializing a milestone, iterating milestone requirements (the mixed-agent loop pass), automated derivation and completion, and ending a milestone, with the draft's "Just put more intelligence and execute" chain folded into the iterating way's intro as the same loop run at maximum effort. The page's headings map one to one onto workflow.md's phase sections and diagram nodes, so a reader moves from the diagram to the chain by heading. Phase names are pipeline structure rather than the goals the template's heading is meant to name, and folding the escalation chain into a sentence drops a goal the milestone goal itself lists as an example together with the six-line chain the draft verified for it.
open-question.recommendation: The goal's list is illustrative and the draft's snippets are what actually ran, so the inventory that ships every draft-chained goal once, in pipeline order, neither invents nor drops a verified chain; under the Host per line layout the two first runs and the Antigravity block collapse into per-line values of the same ways, and fixing the mixed chain as agy review then claude opus recommend and answer copies each line from the snippet that verified it on that host while placing the host swap between review and recommend, so the agent that surfaces the questions is not the agent that recommends on them, which is the mixed-agent review the goal names.
